shortcut_name: reducing the density equation to triangle detection
evidence: gpt-oss-120b uses a bitset adjacency representation and iterates over “neighbours of a that are larger than a”; the defeated solutions also enumerate triples of mutually adjacent vertices
affordance_in_statement: A group of exactly three individuals {a, b, c} justifies the roster failure if the total number of preliminary reports involving at least one of these three individuals is exactly equal to (D_a + D_b + D_c) - 3
removal_suggestion: Re-present the condition through the roster scenario and require verification of the reported-union count and the three individual report totals, rather than exposing the immediately cancellable formula; this can obscure the reduction but cannot eliminate it without changing the underlying task.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Recognizes that the equality holds exactly when all three pairwise reports exist, then searches for the lexicographically smallest triangle using bitset intersections.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: the equality involving the number of reports touching the three people and (D_a + D_b + D_c) - 3

common_affordance: The condition is mathematically equivalent to finding a lexicographically smallest 3-clique (triangle) in the report graph.

defeated_student_causes.why_failed: It enumerates every possible triple with a cubic nested loop, causing TLE at the allowed n bound.
Its implementation performs an inefficient triple-enumeration-style triangle search despite building adjacency and edge sets, causing TLE.
The submitted implementation terminated with a runtime error before producing a valid answer; the available trace does not identify a more specific source line.

recommended_edit: There is no semantics-preserving edit that removes this shortcut: the stated equality intrinsically characterizes a triangle. The only possible presentation edit is to hide the cancellation by describing the union-count and individual-count calculations procedurally in the scenario.
regression_risk: Obscuring the equation could make the already-defeated cubic solutions less likely to recognize triangles, but it cannot reliably defeat a correct bitset triangle algorithm without changing the task.
